<STRUCT_0001>
Note that if <MATH_0001> is surjective and if <MATH_0002> is an Artinian local
<MATH_0003>-algebra, then the identification <MATH_0004>, if it exists,
is unique. Moreover, in this case any <MATH_0005>-algebra map <MATH_0006> is
going to be compatible with the identifications. Hence in this case
<MATH_0007> is just the category of local Artinian <MATH_0008>-algebras
whose residue field ``is'' <MATH_0009>. By abuse of notation we also denote objects of
<MATH_0010> simply <MATH_0011> in the general case. Moreover, we will
often write <MATH_0012>, i.e., we will pretend all rings in
<MATH_0013> have residue field <MATH_0014> (since all ring maps in
<MATH_0015> are compatible with the given identifications this
should never cause any problems).
Throughout the rest of this chapter the base ring <MATH_0016> and the
field <MATH_0017> are fixed. The category <MATH_0018> will be the base
category for the cofibered categories considered below.

Let <MATH_0001> be a ring map in <MATH_0002>.  We say <MATH_0003>
is a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>small extension<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if it is surjective and <MATH_0004> is a nonzero
principal ideal which is annihilated by <MATH_0005>.
